subject: 20 is Plenty
comment: Hello Council Member Fowler, My name is Jacob Kaplefotesn and I'm a Salt Lake City resident living in the Avenues (1251 C ST.). I am also a student in the City and Metropolitan Planning program at the University of Utah. I'm writing to thank you for supporting the "20 is Plenty" ordinance. As a resident, a student, and a cyclist, I strongly think this ordinance will make a major difference in improving the safety of our city's streets. I live near Shirley Park School and I'm constantly struck by the large amount and fast speed of cars throughout our neighborhood, especially with the high volume roads, such as 2700 South and 700 East. Students have to interact with to get to school, I am constantly concerned about their safety. They deserve to have a safe place for those kids, and I'm so grateful for the support on this measure from you and our fellow council members. While the "20 is Plenty" ordinance is a good step in the right direction, we need to make SLC City's streets a safe place for pedestrians, bikers, and other non-car users. We've seen an unfortunate spike in people killed by cars, specifically cyclists, over the last few years. we need to use every asking people to drive slower but fix this problem. We need more impactful solutions, like more traffic calming, road dies, improvements to our intersection design, and other engineering solutions to make a difference and prevent people from being killed by cars on our streets. Our city's transportation department is making great strides in this area, including building protected bike lanes and other measures to help make progress. As our city faces an ongoing climate crisis, I'd encourage you to continue supporting policies that incentivize people to drive less and use more sustainable transportation options. The more people drive more than put out of their cars, Thanks so much for your consideration! I'm happy to provide more information or help answer any other questions you may have. Sincerely, Jacob Kaplefotesn
